title: The Age of Exploration & the Columbian Exchange

pairs.cause: Europeans wanted direct access to Asian spices and goods without paying middlemen.
pairs.effect: Nations funded voyages to find new sea routes to Asia.
pairs.explanation: Cutting out Italian and Muslim traders promised huge profits, so monarchs paid for exploration.

pairs.cause: New tools like the astrolabe, magnetic compass, and caravel improved navigation.
pairs.effect: Sailors could travel farther across open oceans.
pairs.explanation: Better technology made long voyages out of sight of land possible.

pairs.cause: Columbus's voyages linked the Americas with Europe, Africa, and Asia.
pairs.effect: The Columbian Exchange moved plants, animals, people, and diseases between the continents.
pairs.explanation: Permanent contact between the hemispheres set off a massive transfer in both directions.

pairs.cause: Europeans carried diseases like smallpox to the Americas.
pairs.effect: Millions of Indigenous people died from illnesses they had no immunity to.
pairs.explanation: Old World diseases devastated Native populations who had never been exposed to them.

pairs.cause: Colonizers needed labor after Native populations collapsed.
pairs.effect: The transatlantic slave trade expanded enormously.
pairs.explanation: Europeans forced millions of enslaved Africans to the Americas to work plantations and mines.

pairs.cause: American crops like potatoes and maize spread to Europe, Africa, and Asia.
pairs.effect: Populations grew around the world as diets improved.
pairs.explanation: Nutritious, high-yield American crops supported larger populations across the Old World.

pairs.cause: Colonies sent gold, silver, and cash crops back to Europe.
pairs.effect: European nations grew wealthy and competed to build overseas empires.
pairs.explanation: The wealth of empire drove mercantilism and centuries of European colonial expansion.
